answers.why: Israel's outcasts are gathered from among the nations.
Judah's dispersed people are gathered from the four corners of the earth.
Ephraim's envy ends as the scattered peoples are restored and united.
Judah's adversaries are removed in the restoration of the divided peoples.
Ephraim ceases envying Judah, and they subsequently fight neighboring peoples together.
Judah is the people whom Ephraim will no longer envy.
Judah ceases hostility toward Ephraim as the two peoples become united.
Ephraim is the people whom Judah will no longer vex.
Israel's coming up from Egypt recalls the nation's exodus.
The Holy One of Israel dwells among the inhabitants of Zion.
The house of Israel returns to its land and rules over former oppressors.
Fortifications cease from Ephraim in parallel with the kingdom disappearing from Damascus.
The God of Israel announces the survival of a small remnant of the people.
The Holy One of Israel is the nation's God, toward whom people turn from idols.
